title: QUIC Zerortt Hosted Proof Gate Architecture
purpose: Describe the advisory hosted Linux zerortt proof lane that keeps the inventory cell prerequisite-blocked until packet-analysis evidence confirms 0-RTT request-stream data was sent and acted on.
design_summary: The existing server-role zerortt harness path already advertises the early-data and resumption prerequisites, and the manual hosted workflow already exposes the dedicated zerortt-server-proof profile on hosted Linux. The harness now also uses a zerortt-specific request-gap timeout on the resumed second connection so the hosted proof can finish within the runner's network-idle budget. This architecture does not add a new transport branch; it explains the evidence-collection path that keeps the inventory cell blocked until the hosted Linux runner produces packet-analysis proof that 0-RTT request traffic was both sent and acted on. The supporting docs and helper inventory stay explicit so partial hosted success cannot be mistaken for support promotion.
alternatives_considered: Promote zerortt on managed response/download success alone. Rejected because the current runner analysis still requires packet-level 0-RTT proof.
Move zerortt into the major peer matrix. Rejected because the cell is still prerequisite-blocked and the matrix is intentionally scoped to already executable cells.
Introduce a new transport runtime branch. Rejected because the harness and runtime support surface already exists; the remaining work is proof gating and evidence collection.
edge_cases_and_constraints: The hosted Linux profile remains advisory and outside ordinary CI gates.
Windows long-filename runner setup failures stay blocked evidence, not support evidence.
Partial hosted proof, local runtime proof, or server-only dispatch must not upgrade the inventory cell.
data_and_state_considerations: The proof lane relies on preserved runner artifacts under `artifacts/interop-runner/...` and `artifacts/hosted-interop/...`, plus the existing gap ledger and current-status notes. No external runner repository changes are required.
risks: Packet-analysis heuristics may still fail even when the server path and response/download flow are working.
Readers may overread the dedicated hosted profile as support promotion unless the prerequisite-blocked classification stays visible.

supplemental_sections.heading: Scope
supplemental_sections.content: This design only formalizes the remaining zerortt proof gate. It does not change HTTP/3, broad 0-RTT policy, anti-replay, or migration semantics.
